concepts.anchor_rule: Use the midpoint of the longest supported vertical centerline segment, rounded to an integer pixel.
concepts.box_rule: Enclose the supported band segment and a narrow light margin on both sides.
concepts.definition: A locally upright dark band with two approximately parallel sides against a light background.

negatives.evidence: The visible band extends predominantly horizontally.

positives.evidence: The upper part of the visible dark stroke has nearly upright, parallel sides before its lower irregularity.
Below the rounded upper turn, a dark upright segment has light pixels along both sides.

concepts.support_rule: Require both lateral boundaries to be visible over a sustained length. Exclude visibility boundaries from width and termination estimates.

concepts.anchor_rule: Use the midpoint of the longest supported horizontal centerline segment.
concepts.box_rule: Enclose that segment with a narrow light margin above and below.
concepts.definition: A locally horizontal dark band with approximately parallel upper and lower boundaries.

negatives.evidence: The main supported stroke is upright.

positives.evidence: A broad dark strip runs left to right with gently uneven, nearly horizontal boundaries.
A short horizontal section is visible to the left of the downward turn, with light background above and below.

concepts.support_rule: Require visible light background above and below the segment. Cropping at either longitudinal end does not establish a physical endpoint.

concepts.anchor_rule: Use the midpoint of a supported centerline segment with this orientation.
concepts.box_rule: Enclose the diagonal segment and light margins on its two lateral sides.
concepts.definition: An elongated dark band whose centerline rises as it proceeds rightward, allowing small contour irregularities.

negatives.evidence: The visible dark band bends downward as it proceeds rightward.

positives.evidence: A thick diagonal strip climbs from lower left toward upper right.
The visible stroke progresses upward and rightward with uneven sides.
A shallow diagonal dark band rises toward the right across the visible region.

concepts.support_rule: Require two visible lateral boundaries and consistent net upward-right progression. Preserve the slope sign rather than treating both diagonals as equivalent.

concepts.anchor_rule: Use the midpoint of the supported downward-right centerline segment.
concepts.box_rule: Enclose the sloping segment with visible light margins along both sides.
concepts.definition: A dark band whose supported centerline descends toward the right; this candidate remains provisional.

negatives.evidence: The supported diagonal rises toward the right.

positives.evidence: The dark strip starts approximately horizontal and slopes downward toward the right.

concepts.support_rule: Require both lateral contours to support the downward-right direction. Do not use the crop edge as a contour.

concepts.anchor_rule: Use the intersection of fitted centerlines of the incoming and outgoing arms.
concepts.box_rule: Enclose the turn, short supported portions of both arms, and their adjacent inner and outer light regions.
concepts.definition: A dark band entering from the left and turning downward, with a rounded outer upper-right contour and a visible inner recess below-left.

negatives.evidence: The visible elbow connects an upper arm to a rightward lower arm, giving a different orientation.

positives.evidence: The horizontal dark strip turns downward on the right around a visible light inner corner.
A dark arm from the left bends into a descending right-hand arm around a light recess.

concepts.support_rule: Require both arms and evidence of both inner and outer turning contours. A lone convex edge does not establish this elbow.

concepts.anchor_rule: Use the intersection of fitted centerlines of the upper and rightward arms.
concepts.box_rule: Enclose the bend, supported portions of both arms, and light margins around the inner and outer contours.
concepts.definition: A dark band descending from above and turning right, with an inner light recess on the upper-right side of the bend.

negatives.evidence: The light inner recess lies below-left of an upper-right turn.

positives.evidence: An upright stroke turns right at its lower end around a clearly visible light inner corner.
The visible dark stroke descends and rounds into a rightward horizontal section.

concepts.support_rule: Require a visible transition between both arms and a supported inner recess. Do not infer continuation beyond the window.

concepts.anchor_rule: Use the midpoint of the cap across the local stroke width.
concepts.box_rule: Enclose the cap, a short length of its incoming shaft, and the surrounding light margin.
concepts.definition: A dark stroke ending in a visibly rounded downward-facing cap, with light background around the cap.

negatives.evidence: The upright segment reaches the lower visibility boundary without a visible closing cap.

positives.evidence: The descending dark shaft finishes in a rounded lower cap surrounded by white.
Both sides of the lower shaft meet around a rounded, fully visible downward tip.
The right-hand descending arm ends in a rounded cap with visible light beneath it.

concepts.support_rule: Require a continuous visible cap joining both shaft sides and light pixels beyond the downward extremity. A stroke cut by the window cannot supply endpoint evidence.

concepts.anchor_rule: Use the midpoint of the terminal cap measured across the local shaft direction.
concepts.box_rule: Enclose the rounded cap, its supported incoming shaft, and a light margin around the termination.
concepts.definition: A dark stroke ending toward the upper right in a rounded cap, with its shaft extending toward the lower left.

negatives.evidence: The visible rounded termination points downward.

positives.evidence: The short dark protrusion has a rounded upper-right termination surrounded by white.
The branch extending upward and rightward ends in a rounded, visibly bounded tip.

concepts.support_rule: Require visible light beyond the cap and a continuous contour connecting the two shaft sides. Preserve the upper-right terminal orientation.

concepts.anchor_rule: Use the branch attachment point on the fitted centerline of the upright stroke.
concepts.box_rule: Enclose the attachment, supported upright portions above and below it, and the projecting arm.
concepts.definition: A dark upright stroke with an attached arm projecting upward and rightward from its side; this junction candidate remains provisional.

negatives.evidence: The stroke makes a two-arm bend without a visible third arm.

positives.evidence: A narrow upright stroke continues above and below an attached arm that projects toward the upper right.

concepts.support_rule: Require visible continuity of the dark attachment and light wedges separating the branch from the upright stroke above and below. Require evidence of three local directions without inferring hidden continuations.

concepts.anchor_rule: Use the deepest point of the light bay along its opening-to-bottom axis.
concepts.box_rule: Enclose the visible bay, its bordering dark contours, and the supported opening.
concepts.definition: A light region bordered by dark material on its left, right, and lower sides, with a visible opening upward; this candidate remains provisional.

negatives.evidence: The white inner recess opens toward the lower left rather than forming an upward-open bay.

positives.evidence: A central white bay opens upward between dark sides and meets an irregular dark lower boundary.

concepts.support_rule: Require visible side walls and a lower dark boundary while retaining the visible upward opening. Do not infer a closed hole or any contour beyond the crop.
